instruction: Delete all browsing history entries related to Amazon from Chrome.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated Chrome settings to clear Amazon browsing data, cookies, and site data. Also enabled Do Not Track, blocked third-party cookies, and verified Amazon data was removed.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome settings menus, toggle privacy settings, clear browsing data, manage site-specific cookies, use Chrome's privacy and security panel
metadata.task_rationale: Agent demonstrated ability to clear browsing data in the trajectory. This variation focuses specifically on deleting Amazon-related history entries, testing the model's ability to selectively clear history.
metadata.explanation: Task requires deleting Amazon browsing history from Chrome. The config opens Amazon tabs which creates history entries. Evaluator uses official history getter and check_history_deleted metric to verify no Amazon keywords remain in history.

scoring_breakdown.history_deleted: 1.0 - No Amazon-related entries remain in browsing history

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (get_history) correctly reads Chrome's History SQLite DB and returns (url, title, last_visit_time) tuples.
Metric (check_history_deleted) correctly receives the rules dict directly via get_rule and accesses rule['type'] and rule['keywords'] properly.
Keyword 'amazon' will match Amazon URLs since all Amazon pages contain 'amazon' in their URL.
Postconfig properly kills Chrome and relaunches it to release the SQLite DB lock before reading history.
Config correctly creates Amazon history entries by opening Amazon tabs, ensuring there is data to verify deletion of.
Minor: metric only checks URLs (history[0]), not titles (history[1]). An entry with 'amazon' only in title but not URL would be missed, though this is unlikely for Amazon pages.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also checking history titles (history[1]) for the keyword to be more thorough, though for Amazon URLs this is not critical.
